checklist: Pre-purchase inspection at an independent shop (about $150 to $250). Non-negotiable on any private sale.
All four tires must match in brand, model and wear on an AWD car. Mismatched tread strains the AWD system. Budget $600 to $900 if they don't match.
Ask for maintenance records. A folder of receipts is worth real money at this age.
Cold start: ask the seller not to warm it up before you arrive. Listen for rattles or knocks in the first few seconds.
Run the VIN through NHTSA's recall lookup and make sure every open recall is done, especially airbags.
Check the title in person. Name on the title should match the seller's ID.
Portland metro registration needs a DEQ emissions pass. A recent pass is a good sign; ask.
Drive it on the highway and do slow tight turns in a parking lot both directions. Binding, shudder or groaning on turns points to AWD or differential trouble.
teen: IIHS guidance for teen drivers: bigger and heavier is safer, avoid high horsepower, insist on electronic stability control, and pick the best crash ratings you can afford.
Stability control (ESC) is standard on every 2012 and newer car. On older cars, confirm it.
Backup cameras became federally required in May 2018, so 2019+ always has one. Older cars vary by trim.

camera_aftermarket.note: A license-plate camera with a mirror or dash screen runs about $80 to $150 and installs in an afternoon. A new head unit with CarPlay and a camera, installed, runs about $350 to $600 and also adds phone mirroring.

red_flags.label: Branded title
red_flags.detail: Rebuilt or salvage titles hurt resale and insurance, and the damage history is often unknown. Usually skip for a kid's car.

red_flags.re: down ?payment|in[- ]house financ|buy here pay here|bhph|financing available|bad credit|no credit|\$\s?\d[\d,]* down
red_flags.label: Financing dealer
red_flags.detail: Buy-here-pay-here lots often list a down payment or a teaser price. The real price may be higher; ask for the out-the-door cash price.

red_flags.label: Needs work
red_flags.detail: Seller is telling you it needs work. Only worth it if you know exactly what's wrong and the fix is priced in.

red_flags.label: Check engine light
red_flags.detail: Get the code read before going further. Cheap fix or expensive, you need to know.

red_flags.label: Transmission symptom
red_flags.detail: Transmission trouble is the most expensive common failure at this price.

red_flags.re: overheat|blown head gasket|leaking head gasket|head gasket leak|burns oil|smokes
red_flags.label: Engine symptom
red_flags.detail: Overheating, oil burning or a leaking head gasket. Expensive, and a reason to pass unless priced as a project.

red_flags.label: Flood mention
red_flags.detail: Flood cars develop electrical problems for years. Pass.

red_flags.label: Modified
red_flags.detail: Modified cars tend to have been driven hard, and mods can complicate insurance and DEQ.

red_flags.label: AC not working
red_flags.detail: "Just needs a recharge" is often a leak or a failing compressor, $800 to $2,000. Assume the expensive version until a shop says otherwise.

green_flags.re: service records|maintenance records|all records|records available|dealer maintained
green_flags.label: Has records

4Matic at this price is a project car.

issues.title: Head gaskets (EJ25)
issues.detail: External oil and coolant leaks from the head gaskets. Repair is $1,800 to $2,800 and usually includes the timing belt.
issues.check: Ask if head gaskets were done and get the receipt. Look under the engine for oil or coolant weeping at the seam where the heads meet the block. Sweet smell after a drive is coolant.

issues.detail: EJ25 uses a timing belt due about every 105k miles. Often done with head gaskets.

issues.title: Oil consumption (FB25)

issues.check: Pull the dipstick: low or very dark oil is a warning. Ask if the engine was ever replaced or tested for consumption.

issues.title: CVT
issues.detail: Subaru's CVT can shudder or whine as it ages. Subaru extended CVT coverage on early years, now expired.
issues.check: Ask for CVT fluid service records. On the drive, accelerate gently from a stop and listen for whine or judder.

issues.title: Wheel bearings
issues.detail: Rear wheel bearings wear out; a growl that changes with speed.
issues.check: Listen at 30 to 50 mph for a hum that changes when you weave slightly.

issues.title: Battery drain
issues.detail: Some 2015+ Subarus had a parasitic battery drain (subject of a class action).
issues.check: Ask if the battery has been replaced more than once.

checklist: Look at the coolant reservoir for oily film.
